h: Faith and the Renewed Divine Image

p: "יְשַׁדַּר לָן שׁוּפְרֵיהּ וְנֶחזֵי בִיקָרֵיהּ וְיַחזֵי לָן סִתְרֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי".
— “May He transmit to us His radiant beauty, and we shall gaze upon His glory, and He shall reveal to us His hidden mysteries, etc.” (from the Shabbat hymn Azamer Bishvachin).
הִנֵּה הוּא בַּקָּשָׁה עַל הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
— Behold, this is a supplication for the revelation of Atika Kadisha (the Ancient Holy One),
שֶׁעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז "וְיַחזֵי לָן סִתְרֵיהּ" – הַיְינוּ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
— which is alluded to by “and He shall reveal to us His hidden mysteries”—namely the revelation of Atik,
כִּדְאִיתָא (פְּסָחִים קיט.):
— as it is stated in Pesachim (119a):
"וְלִמְכַסֶּה עָתִיק" (יְשַׁעְיָה כג, יח) –
— “And for stately / hidden covering” (Isaiah 23:18) –
זֶה הַמְכַסֶּה דְּבָרִים שֶׁכִּסָּה עַתִּיק יוֹמִין,
— this refers to one who conceals matters that the Ancient of Days covered,
וּמַאי נִיהוּ? סִתְרֵי תוֹרָה;
— and what are they? The esoteric secrets of the Torah;
וְכֵן "יְשַׁדַּר לָן שׁוּפְרֵיהּ" גַּם כֵּן מְרַמֵּז עַל עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא.
— and likewise “may He transmit to us His radiant beauty” also alludes to the Ancient Holy One.
וְאֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא?
— Now how could it be conceivable to plead for the revelation of Atika?
הֲלֹא הוּא שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן וְלֵית מַחֲשָׁבָה תְּפִיסָא בֵּיהּ כְּלָל!
— Is He not the Intellect concealed from all contemplation, Whom no mortal thought can grasp whatsoever!
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קפח עַמּוּד א)
— And in the holy Zohar in this Parashah (188a) it is taught
דְּהַפּוֹגֵם בְּרִית לָא חָמֵי סְבַר אַפֵּי עַתִּיק יוֹמִין, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
— that whoever blemishes the holy covenant does not behold the welcoming countenance of the Ancient of Days, see there,
מַשְׁמָע דְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא פָּגַם חָמֵי!
— implying that one who has not blemished does behold Him!
וְאֵיךְ יוּכַל שׁוּם נִבְרָא לִרְאוֹתוֹ,
— Yet how could any created being ever see Him,
וְהוּא נֶעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן,
— when He is utterly concealed from all human conception,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אֵל מִסְתַּתֵּר וְכוּלֵי, הַשֵּׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן וְכוּלֵי מֻכְתָּר בְּכֶתֶר עֶלְיוֹן"?
— and as chanted: “God Who conceals Himself, the Intellect hidden from all contemplation, crowned with the Supreme Crown”?
וּבְפָרָשַׁת וַיְחִי (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, ריט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) אִיתָא:
— And in Parashat Vayechi (Zohar Part I, 219b end) it states:
"וְלָא חָמֵי אַפֵּי שְׁכִינְתָּא", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
— “and he does not behold the face of the Shechinah,” see there,
וְזֶה הַמַּדְרֵגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה – מִדַּת מַלְכוּת הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— and this represents the final sefirotic level—the attribute of Malchut that dwells amidst the children of Israel.
אֲבָל יָדוּעַ מִמַּאֲמַר 'פָּתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ':
— However, it is known from the passage Patach Eliyahu:
כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן אִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת וְכוּלֵי,
— “Keter Elyon is the crown of Malchut, etc.,”
הַמַּגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית.
— linking the ultimate Beginning with the final End.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 119a: “The Gemara asks: What is the meaning of the continuation of this verse: ‘For stately clothing (limekhaseh atik)’ This is one who conceals (mekhaseh) matters that the Ancient of Days (atik yomin), i.e., God, concealed. And what are these? These are the secrets of the Torah, the esoteric Act of Creation and the Act of the Divine Chariot, which should remain hidden. And some say: This verse is referring to one who reveals matters that the Ancient of Days concealed. And what are these? These are the reasons for different mitzvot in the Torah, which should be kept secret.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayechi 23:182-26:195: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others. Come and see: once ‘Woe to the wicked one’ is written, why add ‘evil’? As explained, he made himself evil. ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’: others ascend, but he does not. What of other sinners who killed people? They all ascend, but he does not. They killed other people; he killed his own children, shedding much blood. Of other sinners it does not say ‘What he did was evil in the Lord’s eyes,’ but here it does, because ‘he wasted it upon the earth.’ Rabbi Yehudah taught: there is no offense in the world without repentance except this one, and no sinners who fail to behold the Shekhinah’s face except this one, as in ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’—at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come: ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ What is this inheritance? As in ‘I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living.’”

h: The Image of the Divine Face

p: וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן "יְשַׁדַּר לָן שׁוּפְרֵיהּ" – הַיְינוּ הַפָּנִים,
— And this is the phrasing “may He transmit to us His radiant beauty”—referring to the Countenance;
וְאֵיךְ יִתָּכֵן לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּשְׁלַח הַפָּנִים,
— and how could it be said that He “transmit” the face,
וְהָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לָנוּ הַפָּנִים?
— when it should properly have said that He “show” us the face?
אַךְ הַפֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁיִּשְׁלַח כְּמוֹ מִי שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ צוּרַת הַפָּנִים שֶׁלּוֹ
— Rather the meaning is: that He transmit just like one who sends a portrait of his face
מְצוּיֶּרֶת עַל הַטַּבְלָא אוֹ עַל הַנְּיָיר.
— depicted upon a tablet or upon parchment.
וְכֵן הָעִנְיָן "אַפֵּי שְׁכִינְתָּא",
— And likewise is the concept of “the face of the Shechinah”:
כִּי שְׁכִינְתָּא אִיהִי אֱמוּנָה
— for the Shechinah is the attribute of Faith
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רל עַמּוּד א),
— (as written in Zohar Part III, 230a),
וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת מַלְכוּת דִּכְתִיב: "אֲנִי ה' שֹׁכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" (בַּמִּדְבָּר לה, לד).
— and this is the attribute of Malchut concerning which it is written: “I am Hashem Who dwells amidst the children of Israel” (Numbers 35:34).
וּכְנֶגֶד מִדָּה זוֹ שֵׁם אֲדֹנָ"י,
— And corresponding to this attribute is the divine Name Adonut,
שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ אָדוֹן בָּעוֹלָם וְהוּא מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם וַאֲנַחְנוּ עַמּוֹ,
— for Israel are believers the children of believers that there is a Master in the universe, the Sovereign of the world, and we are His people,
וּמִצַּד אֱמוּנָה אֲנַחְנוּ מַשִּׂיגִים כְּבוֹד אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
— and through the portal of faith we perceive the glory of His divinity, blessed be His Name.
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא בְּשַׁבָּת,
— And the overt revelation of Malchut occurs on Shabbat,
שֶׁהִיא מִדָּה שְׁבִיעִית, מִדַּת מַלְכוּת.
— which is the seventh sefirotic attribute, Malchut.
וְאָמְנָם הִתְגַּלּוּת הַמַּלְכוּת לֹא יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
— However, the disclosure of Sovereignty cannot be fully complete
רַק כְּשֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ מוּכְתָּר בְּכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת,
— except when the Sovereign is crowned with the royal Crown,
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז "מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית" – כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן אִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת.
— and this is what is hinted in “Declaring the end from the beginning”—Keter Elyon is the crown of Malchut.
וּמִצַּד אֱמוּנָה בְּשַׁבָּת, שֶׁהִיא בְּיֶתֶר הִתְגַּלּוּת,
— And by virtue of faith on Shabbat, which is in heightened revelation,
יְכוֹלִים לְהַשִּׂיג כְּבוֹד אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ גַּם מֵעֵין עַתִּיקָא,
— we can comprehend the glory of His divinity, blessed be His Name, even as an emanation of Atika,
זוּלַת מִי שֶׁפָּגַם בְּרִיתוֹ.
— excepting one who has blemished his covenant.
וְשַׁבָּת בְּרָזָא דִּבְרִית,
— For Shabbat embodies the mystery of the Covenant,
דְּשַׁבָּת הוּא תִּיקּוּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— in that Shabbat provides the spiritual rectification for the blemish of the covenant,
וְיֵשׁ יְכוֹלֶת לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל הַחֲפֵצִים לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמָם בְּשַׁבָּת
— and there is power for all Jews who yearn to sanctify themselves on Shabbat
וּלְהִתְקָרֵב לִקְדוּשָׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
— and draw close to His holiness, blessed be He,
לְהַגִּיעַ לְהַשָּׂגַת סְבַר אַפֵּי עַתִּיק יוֹמִין.
— to attain the grasp of the welcoming Countenance of the Ancient of Days.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Pinchas, III 230a; 53:332: “The masters of the Mishnah therefore established: ‘Study is not the main thing, but action.’ For the Holy One is concealed in the secrets of Torah. Through what is He made known? Through the commandments, which are His Shekhinah, His likeness. As He is humble, His Shekhinah is humility; He is pious, and she is pious; He is mighty, and she rules over all the nations of the world. He is Truth, and she is Faith; He is Prophet, and she is prophecy; He is Righteous, and she is righteousness; He is King, and she is Sovereignty…” The words ‘He is Truth, and she is Faith’ explicitly identify the Shekhinah with faith. p: וְהִנֵּה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
— Now King David, peace be upon him, who is the chariot for Malchut which corresponds to the Sabbath day,
וְהוּא הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה לְכָל הַפְּגָמִים
— and who established the yoke of repentance for all moral blemishes,
וְאַף לִפְגָם זֶה שֶׁמַּחְמִיר הַרְבֵּה בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— and even for this covenantal sin upon which the holy Zohar is exceedingly severe,
הִתְפַּלֵּל: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי אֱלֹהִים" (תְּהִלִּים נא, יב),
— he prayed: “Create in me a clean heart, O God” (Psalms 51:12),
וְאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב.): מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא טָמֵא,
— and they said in Sukkah (52a): this implies that an impure heart exists;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲזִיק עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא מְרוּחָק מֵהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הָרִיחוּק
— meaning that he held himself to be alienated from the Holy One in absolute distance,
מִצַּד שֶׁהַלֵּב שֶׁלּוֹ אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם תִּקְוָה שֶׁתּוּכַל לְהִטָּהֵר וּלְהִתְקָרֵב לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
— believing that his heart possessed no natural prospect of self-purification to draw close to holiness,
וְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה לוֹ בְּרִיאָה חֲדָשָׁה,
— and he prayed to the Holy One that He fashion for him a brand new creation,
שֶׁיִּבְרָא לוֹ לֵב טָהוֹר יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן.
— that He create for him a pure heart ex nihilo (something from nothing).
"וְרוּחַ נָכוֹן חַדֵּשׁ בְּקִרְבִּי" (שָׁם),
— “And renew a steadfast spirit within me” (ibid.),
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קצב עַמּוּד ב):
— as brought in the holy Zohar in this Parashah (192b):
"וְרוּחַ נָכוֹן וְגוֹמֵר" – דָּא הוּא רוּחַ נָכוֹן וַדַּאי,
— “and a steadfast spirit, etc.”—this is certainly the steadfast spirit,
כְּדִכְתִיב: "וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב)
— as it is written: “and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters” (Genesis 1:2)
וְאִתְעָרוּ: זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ;
— and they awakened the teaching: this is the spirit of the Messiah;
וְאִתְעָרוּ: "וְרוּחַ חֲדָשָׁה אֶתֵּן בְּקִרְבְּכֶם" (יְחֶזְקֵאל לו, כו),
— and they awakened the verse: “and a new spirit will I put within you” (Ezekiel 36:26),
וְצַלֵּי דָּוִד הַהוּא רוּחַ נָכוֹן: "חַדֵּשׁ בְּקִרְבִּי וְכוּלֵי".
— and David prayed for that steadfast spirit: “renew within me, etc.”
מַאי "חַדֵּשׁ"?
— What is the meaning of “renew”?
דָּא חִדּוּשָׁא דְּסִיהֲרָא,
— This is the renewal of the moon,
בְּשַׁעְתָּא דְּאִתְחַדַּשׁ סִיהֲרָא: "דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל חַי וְקַיָּם",
— for at the hour when the moon is renewed we proclaim: “David, King of Israel, is alive and enduring,”
וּבְגִין כָּךְ "חַדֵּשׁ".
— and on this account he said “renew”.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Malbim, Tehillim 51:12: “‘A pure heart’: sin comes through desire, which stems from matter, while iniquity comes through a distortion of the intellect or spirit, which raises images to the heart, and it raises evil images inclined toward wrong. One who does not sin has a pure heart, and one who does not distort has a steadfast spirit. The heart denotes the outer, material vessel in which the spirit dwells, and the spirit is the inner power of the soul. Purity of heart means that matter has no inclination or desire toward evil; a steadfast spirit means that the inner spirit raises before the soul only images of truth and goodness. Now the heart that is not pure is so from birth, but the spirit that is not steadfast is not: matter by its nature has an inclination toward desire, so that if Hashem wishes to repair it so that it will not desire evil, a new creation is required. Thus he said, ‘Create in me a pure heart, O God’: that He create his heart as a new creation that will no longer desire evil. But the spirit is not distorted from birth, for the soul from its root and beginning is prepared to depict only truth and goodness, and the distortion arises in a person afterwards. One needs only that Hashem renew within him a steadfast spirit as the soul was at first, and thus he said, ‘and renew a steadfast spirit within me.’”

p: הַיְינוּ כִּי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא מָשִׁיחַ
— This means that King David, peace be upon him, desired that he himself be the final Messiah
וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה קֵץ הַגְּאוּלָּה בְּיָמָיו,
— and that the ultimate redemption unfold in his own days,
שֶׁכֵּן הִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה בְּיָמָיו לְעִנְיָן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד,
— for he prayed that he merit in his lifetime that spiritual reality destined for the future,
וְהַיְינוּ: "וְרוּחַ חֲדָשָׁה אֶתֵּן בְּקִרְבְּכֶם" – זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ
— namely: “and a new spirit will I put within you”—which is the spirit of King Messiah
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא,
— which alludes to the supreme revelation of Atika,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדָנִיֵּאל (ז, יג) עַל מָשִׁיחַ:
— as written in Daniel (7:13) regarding the Messiah:
"עִם עֲנָנֵי שְׁמַיָּא כִּבְרַ אֱנָשׁ אָתֵה הֲוָה,
— “with the clouds of heaven one like the son of man came,
וְעַד עַתִּיק יוֹמַיָּא מְטָה וּקְדָמוֹהִי הַקְרְבוּהִי".
— and he arrived even unto the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before Him.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּרוּמָּז בְּמַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית",
— And as alluded to in the primal utterance of Bereishit,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לב.):
— concerning which they taught (Rosh Hashanah 32a):
"בְּרֵאשִׁית" נַמֵּי מַאֲמָר הוּא,
— “Bereishit” is also an utterance,
וְלֹא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ "וַיֹּאמֶר" בְּפֵירוּשׁ,
— yet “and He said” is not explicitly written in it,
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל עַתִּיקָא, שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם;
— hinting to Atika, the pristine Concealed Intellect;
וּכְתִיב בּוֹ: "וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם",
— and concerning it Scripture writes: “and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters”,
וְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (ב, ד):
— and it is stated in Bereishit Rabbah (2:4):
זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ וְכוּלֵי;
— this is the spirit of King Messiah, etc.;
בְּאֵיזוֹ זְכוּת?
— by what merit?
בִּזְכוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנֶּמְשְׁלָה כְּמַיִם,
— by the merit of repentance which is compared to water,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שִׁפְכִי כַמַּיִם לִבֵּךְ" (אֵיכָה ב, יט).
— as it is stated: “Pour out your heart like water” (Lamentations 2:19).
כִּי הוּא יִהְיֶה יָחִיד שֶׁעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמּוֹחֲלִין לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ
— For he will be the unique individual whose repentance is so vast that the whole world is forgiven through him
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא פו:),
— (as written in Yoma 86b),
וְהַיְינוּ מִצַּד שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ יִתֵּן רוּחַ תְּשׁוּבָה בְּלֵב כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָשׁוּבוּ כֻּלָּם.
— meaning that King Messiah will infuse the spirit of teshuvah into the hearts of all Jewish souls so that all return.

p: וּכְתִיב: "וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב חָדָשׁ" (יְחֶזְקֵאל לו, כו),
— And it is written: “A new heart also will I give you” (Ezekiel 36:26),
וּלְמַעְלָה כְּתִיב: "וְנָתַתִּי לָהֶם לֵב אֶחָד" (שָׁם יא, יט),
— and earlier it is written: “And I will give them one heart” (ibid. 11:19),
וְהַיְינוּ הַלֵּב חָדָשׁ,
— and this is synonymous with the new heart;
שֶׁאֵיךְ יִתָּכֵן שֶׁיִּתֵּן לֵב אֶחָד לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל?
— for how could it literally be that He give one single physical heart to all Israel?
אַךְ הַפֵּירוּשׁ הוּא:
— Rather the explanation is:
שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיֶה לָהֶם רַק לֵב אֶחָד לַאֲבִינוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם,
— that all Israel will possess only one undivided heart directed to our Father in Heaven,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בִּלְבָבָם שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה
— harboring in their hearts no extraneous thoughts whatsoever,
רַק יִהְיֶה לִבָּם מָלֵא תְּשׁוּקָה וְרָצוֹן רַק לִרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— their heart being filled solely with longing and yearning for His will, blessed be He.
וְגַם הַ"לֵּב כְּסִיל" יִתְמַלֵּא בְּרָצוֹן לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
— And even “the heart of the fool” on the left will be filled with desire to perform His will,
וְיִהְיוּ הַשְּׁנֵי לְבָבוֹת לֵב אֶחָד,
— and the two inclinations will become a single unified heart,
כְּמוֹ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּתַכְלִית מְכֻוָּון הַבְּרִיאָה כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל,
— just as at the Giving of the Torah when Israel achieved the ultimate intent of Creation like Adam before the fall,
וּכְתִיב: "וַיִּחַן שָׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל" (שְׁמוֹת יט, ב),
— and it is written: “and there Israel encamped” (Exodus 19:2),
וְאִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא: כָּאן הִשְׁווּ לֵב אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי.
— and it is brought in the Mekhilta: here they unified as one heart, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ מִצַּד שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בִּלְבָבָם שׁוּם רָצוֹן אַחֵר זוּלַת לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ,
— And this was because they possessed no other desire other than to execute His will, blessed be His Name,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כֹּל אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר ה' נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע" (שָׁם כד, ז),
— and as stated: “All that Hashem has spoken we will do and hear” (ibid. 24:7),
שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ עֲשִׂיָּה לִשְׁמִיעָה מִצַּד שֶׁהָיָה לֵב כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— prioritizing action over hearing because the heart of all Israel was focused purely on doing His will.

p: וְאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "מַאי חַדֵּשׁ? דָּא חִדּוּשָׁא דְּסִיהֲרָא וְכוּלֵי",
— And the holy Zohar stated: “What is 'renew'? This is the renewal of the moon, etc.”,
וְהוּא, דִּכְמוֹ שֶׁהַלְּבָנָה מִתְחַדֶּשֶׁת תָּמִיד וּמְקַבֶּלֶת תָּמִיד אוֹר חָדָשׁ,
— and this means: just as the moon continuously renews itself and continually receives fresh light,
כָּךְ מִתְחַדֵּשׁ תָּמִיד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַלֵּב חָדָשׁ וְרוּחַ חֲדָשָׁה,
— so too is the new heart and new spirit continuously renewed within Israel,
שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין תָּמִיד הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת אוֹר שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים הַשָּׂגָה חֲדָשָׁה בִּכְבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ וֵאלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
— perpetually receiving an influx of light whereby they attain fresh perceptions of His Sovereignty and divinity
מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא אֵין סוֹף.
— emanating from the disclosure of Atika which is without end.
וּבְשַׁבָּת יְכוֹלִים לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַפְּגָמִים מִצַּד הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת רוּחַ חֲדָשָׁה,
— And on Shabbat one can rectify all flaws through the renewal of this new spirit,
כִּי בְּכָל שַׁבָּת הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה חֲדָשָׁה,
— for on each Shabbat the additional soul is entirely new,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁלְּכָךְ נִקְרֵאת בְּכָל שַׁבָּת "כַּלָּה"
— as we noted: this is why on every Shabbat it is titled “Bride”,
כִּי הִיא חֲדָשָׁה בְּכָל שַׁבָּת בְּמַדְרֵגָה חֲדָשָׁה מִשַּׁבָּתוֹת שֶׁעָבְרוּ.
— because it arrives renewed each Sabbath on an elevated rung beyond past Sabbaths.
וּנְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה – נִשְׁמָתָא דְּכָל שְׁלִימוּ בָּהּ כְּדוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי
— And the additional soul—a soul possessing all perfection modeled after the World to Come
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, פח עַמּוּד ב),
— (as written in the holy Zohar Part II, 88b),
וְהוּא מֵרוּחוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ בְּכֹחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
— and it is drawn from the spirit of King Messiah through the power of repentance.
וְגַם בְּשַׁבָּת מִתְחַדֵּשׁ הַלֵּב אֶחָד
— And on Shabbat the single unified heart is likewise renewed,
שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— wherein our true desire is solely to perform His will, blessed be He,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קיח:):
— as they said (Shabbat 118b):
"הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ וְכוּלֵי";
— “Whoever delights in the Sabbath is granted the desires of his heart, etc.”;
וְאִיתָא בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב (מִזְמוֹר כ, ו):
— and it is brought in Shocher Tov (Psalm 20:6):
"יְמַלֵּא ה' כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹתֶיךָ" –
— “May Hashem fulfill all your petitions” –
זוֹ תְּפִלָּה שֶׁאֵין מִתְפַּלְּלִין עַל כָּל אָדָם,
— this is a prayer that one does not pray for every person,
לְפִי שֶׁפְּעָמִים יֵשׁ בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם לִגְנוֹב וְכוּלֵי,
— because sometimes there resides in a person’s heart the desire to steal, etc.,
אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ שָׁלֵם לִפְנֵי בּוֹרְאוֹ וְכוּלֵי.
— rather only for one whose heart is wholly pure before his Creator, etc.
וְכָאן אָמַר שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ,
— Yet here regarding Shabbat it states that he is granted his heart’s desires unconditionally,
וְהַטַּעַם: שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל רַק לְטוֹבָה לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
— and the reason is: on Shabbat the desires of the heart of Israel are directed purely toward the good, to execute His will, blessed be His Name.

p: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קעט עַמּוּד ב):
— And in the holy Zohar at the opening of this Parashah (179b):
"יֶלֶד מִסְכֵּן" (קֹהֶלֶת ד, יג) – דָּא אִיהוּ יֵצֶר טוֹב,
— “A poor child” (Ecclesiastes 4:13)—this is the good inclination,
וְדָא הוּא "נַעַר" וְכוּלֵי,
— and this is the “youth” (na'ar), etc.,
בְּגִין דְּאִית לֵיהּ חַדְתּוּ דְּסִיהֲרָא דְּמִתְחַדְּשָׁא תָּדִיר וְכוּלֵי.
— because he partakes in the renewal of the moon which renews continually, etc.
וְזֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל חִדּוּשֵׁי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— And this alludes to innovative novellae of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
— for through constant innovation in the Oral Torah and diligent immersion in Torah
יוּכַל הָאָדָם גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַפְּגָמִים,
— a person is likewise empowered to rectify all spiritual blemishes;
וְזֶהוּ "חַדְתּוּתָא דְּסִיהֲרָא"
— and this is the “renewal of the moon”
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁמְּקַבֶּלֶת הַשְׁפָּעַת אוֹר מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
— which alludes to the Oral Torah which receives its radiant illumination from the Written Torah.
וְהַלְּבָנָה נִקְרֵאת גַּם כֵּן "יֶלֶד" – לְשׁוֹן לֵידָה,
— And the moon is likewise called “child” (yeled)—an expression of birth (leidah),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ:):
— as we find in Rosh Hashanah (20b):
נוֹלַד קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת אוֹ נוֹלַד אַחַר חֲצוֹת,
— whether it was born before midday or born after midday,
וְכֵן (שָׁם כה.): "וּלְמָחָר כְּרֵיסָהּ בֵּין שִׁנֶּיהָ",
— and likewise (ibid. 25a): “and tomorrow its belly is between its teeth”,
וְנִקְרָא מוֹלַד הַלְּבָנָה.
— and it is titled the birth/conjunction of the moon (molad).
וּכְמוֹ כֵן הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב נִקְרָא "יֶלֶד",
— And similarly the good inclination is titled “child”,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ:
— as written in the holy Zohar:
בְּגִין דְּאִית לֵיהּ חַדְתּוּ דְּסִיהֲרָא דְּמִתְחַדְּשָׁא תָּדִיר,
— because he possesses the renewal of the moon that is continually renewed,
וְתָדִיר אִיהוּ יֶלֶד כִּי נוֹלָד בְּכָל פַּעַם לֵידָה חֲדָשָׁה בְּהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— and he is perpetually a child because at every moment he is born afresh through the renewal of the Oral Torah.
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא גַּם כֵּן זְמַן הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
— And Shabbat is likewise the supreme time for innovation in Torah novellae,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק א):
— as written at the opening of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 1):
שַׁבָּת יֵעָשֶׂה כֻּלּוֹ תוֹרָה.
— Shabbat should be made entirely Torah.

The renewal of the world at that time follows the renewal among the souls of Israel in each generation, as they said in Yevamot: even ships are for the sake of Israel. paragraphs.text: Connection: The “new birth” here is grounded in a reciprocal relation between Torah and the soul. The character of each generation opens new Torah, and the new Torah in turn brings new soul-life to expression. The present renewal therefore concerns the person who learns as well as the teaching that is learned.
